title: You Don’t Need Aligned Representations: Knowledge Distillation via Random Prototype Spaces
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: Prior distillation aligns student features to a task-sized space with learned projectors; ours aligns both networks through a frozen shared random prototype space.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, left-to-right flow, teacher on top and student on bottom
description: Two side-by-side panels compare OFA (a) with RPKD (b). In both, a cat photo on the left feeds a blue Teacher bar on top and a pink Student bar on the bottom. Each network outputs a small stacked-cell logit vector on the right. In (a), four gray Proj boxes hang off the student, with dashed arrows going up to dark L_OFA and L_KD loss nodes. In (b), a purple translucent sphere of prototype points, labeled P in R^{M×R}, sits between the networks. Frozen teacher maps φ_t^f and φ_t^g, marked with snowflakes, feed it from above. Learnable student maps φ_s^f and φ_s^g, marked with flames, feed it from below. Dark L_feat and L_logit nodes sit left and right of the sphere. An orange box on the far right sums them into the RPKD Loss. The sphere draws the eye first.
caption: Method comparison: OFA vs.\ RPKD. (a) OFA places four learned Proj modules at intermediate student stages, each mapping student features into the shared class logit space ($C$-dimensional) for stage-wise alignment with the teacher's output distribution; projectors are trained jointly and are architecture-specific. (b) RPKD transfers knowledge through a frozen random prototype matrix $P\!\in\!\mathbb{R}^{M\times R}$, fixed at initialization and shared by both networks. The teacher projects into $P$ via frozen random linear maps $\phi_t^{\mathrm{g}}, \phi_t^{\mathrm{f}}$ (\raisebox{-1pt}{\includegraphics[height=8pt]snow} frozen), requiring no teacher-side updates. The student adapts via learnable MLP projectors $\phi_s^{\mathrm{g}}, \phi_s^{\mathrm{f}}$ (\raisebox{-1pt}{\includegraphics[height=8pt]fire} learnable) to match the teacher's prototype similarity patterns. Two complementary branches are optimized alongside the task cross-entropy: $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{logit}}$ (global prototype similarity) and $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{feat}}$ (spatial prototype activation maps). Unlike OFA, whose projectors target a space whose width is set by the task, RPKD keeps the prototype bank and both losses unchanged across pairs; only the two input projections are sized to each network's feature width.
abstract: A widely held assumption in knowledge distillation is that teacher and student representations must occupy a compatible or explicitly aligned feature space. We propose RPKD (Random Prototype Knowledge Distillation), which discards this assumption by comparing both networks against a shared bank of randomly initialized, frozen prototype vectors. Alignment is therefore carried out in an external reference space rather than in the teacher's native feature coordinates: the teacher side is projected by fixed random maps that carry no trainable parameters, and only the student adapts. Two branches handle the transfer: a logit branch aligning global prototype similarity distributions and a feature branch matching spatially-resolved prototype activation maps. Both operate within the same fixed prototype space, which can be interpreted as a random feature embedding that approximately preserves inter-sample similarity structure, so the prototype bank and the distillation objective stay unchanged across teacher-student pairs while only the input projections are instantiated per architecture. In low-category settings, decoupling the prototype vocabulary from the task label space yields richer supervision than the label space alone, an advantage absent from logit-based methods, whose supervisory signal collapses as class count shrinks. This advantage is especially relevant in real-world scenarios where the label space is typically constrained. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of RPKD, achieving a maximum gain of +7.98% over OFA on CIFAR-100, +12.44% on ImageNet-100, and +1.28% on ImageNet-1K. Source code is available at https://github.com/HamzaEtcibasi/RPKD
